questions.question: What are the elements of the symmetric group $S_n$?
questions.explanation: The symmetric group $S_n$ consists of every bijection from an $n$-element set to itself, i.e. all of its permutations.
questions.source_support: Definition: $S_n$ is the set of all permutations of an $n$-element set.

questions.question: Why is $(S_n,\circ)$ a group?
options: Every permutation sends all objects to the same object, for every possible choice of input.
Permutation composition has closure, associativity, an identity permutation, and inverse permutations
Composition of permutations is always commutative
questions.explanation: Composition of permutations is closed and associative, the identity fixes every element, and reversing a bijection gives an inverse. These are exactly the group axioms.
